subject.title: [Feature]: Browser sandbox should support non-Docker backends (external CDP/noVNC endpoint)

question: Should sandbox-browser external endpoint support be added as narrow config fields, designed as a backend/provider contract first, or kept Docker-only until the broader browser backend API is settled?
rationale: The implementation shape controls public config, CDP/noVNC authority, browser lifecycle ownership, and sandbox isolation guarantees, so code inspection cannot safely choose it without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design endpoint contract first
options.body: Define a typed sandbox-browser backend/external-endpoint contract with auth, SSRF, noVNC, lifecycle, docs, and tests before adding public config fields.

options.title: Add narrow endpoint fields
options.body: This would unblock sidecar/CDP deployments faster but risks locking in an underdesigned security and configuration surface.

options.title: Fold into browser-backend API work
options.body: This keeps core lean but should explicitly preserve this issue's sandbox-browser lifecycle and noVNC/CDP requirements in the broader design.

recommendation.title: Design endpoint contract first
recommendation.body: Define a typed sandbox-browser backend/external-endpoint contract with auth, SSRF, noVNC, lifecycle, docs, and tests before adding public config fields.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history is on sandbox browser behavior, backend documentation, and security-sensitive sandbox policy surfaces.
